rounds.text: Sumax Engineering Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a modest P/E of 18.9 [E1] with a striking margin of safety of 60.4% relative to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 280 per share [E29, E30]. The business generates exceptional capital returns, boasting an ROCE of 23.85% to 25.2% [E9, E11] and an ROE of 20.2% to 20.71% [E8, E12], both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Operational quality is rising steadily, evidenced by operating margins expanding by 6 percentage points to 12% in March 2026 alongside a multi-year increasing margin trend [E19, E20], backed by strong cash conversion of 1.46x where operating cash flow reached Rs 19 Cr [E21, E22]. Growth momentum remains firmly intact via robust 3-year compounded profit growth of 36% [E15] supported by a supportive sector tailwind in Automobile & Auto Components with a score of +0.63 [E40, E41]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price only prices in a modest 5.3% earnings growth rate [E31], and the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.21x [E25]. Conceded: free cash flow stands at Rs -8 Cr in March 2026 [E23], borrowings increased to Rs 13 Cr [E26], and the company was flagged for potentially capitalizing interest costs [E34].

Despite healthy headline returns, Sumax Engineering Ltd exhibits a severe deceleration in top-line growth, with compounded sales dropping to 5% over 3 years and stalling at a mere 1% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14]. This stagnation occurs against a sector median sales growth of 20.6%, highlighting that the company is lagging far behind its industry peers [E43]. Furthermore, despite reporting solid operating cash flow of Rs 19 Cr in March 2026, the company generated negative free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr during the same period, driven by an increase in borrowings to Rs 13 Cr from Rs 8 Cr the previous year [E22, E23, E26]. Compounding these liquidity concerns, filed statements flag a critical negative risk: the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E34]. Finally, shareholders receive zero return in cash, as the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E7, E9, E11, E12, E19, E20, E21, E24, E25, E29, E30, E31, E36, E37, E38, E39, E40, E41, E42, E44].

While sales growth has slowed [E13, E14], the company has successfully prioritized efficiency, achieving a 36% compounded profit growth over three years [E15] and doubling its operating margin to 12% [E19, E20]. The negative free cash flow [E23] and modest increase in borrowings [E26] are offset by a very conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x [E25] and exceptional cash generation, where operating cash flow represents 132% of operating profit [E24]. Concerns regarding interest capitalization [E34] are mitigated by the fact that profits are fully backed by cash at a 1.46x conversion rate [E21] and the company delivers a 25.2% ROCE, which is nearly double the sector median [E11, E44]. Conceded: [E3, E14, E43]. However, the lack of dividends is outweighed by a massive 60.4% margin of safety [E30], with the current market price of Rs 111 trading at a steep discount to the Rs 280 intrinsic value [E29]. Finally, the current price only implies a 5.3% earnings growth rate [E31], which is easily achievable given the company's 13% trailing twelve-month profit growth [E16].

Conceded: [E13], [E15], [E19], [E20], [E21], [E24], [E25], [E29], [E30], [E31], [E44]. However, the company's growth momentum has severely stalled, with trailing twelve-month sales growth collapsing to just 1% [E14]—vastly underperforming the sector median sales growth of 20.6% [E43]—and trailing twelve-month profit growth slowing to 13% [E16], which is below the sector median of 15.7% [E42]. These growth figures do not offset the reality of a deeply negative free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr [E23] and a sharp increase in borrowings from Rs 8 Cr to Rs 13 Cr [E26]. Furthermore, the serious red flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E34] casts doubt on the integrity of its reported profitability, meaning the celebrated 25.2% ROCE [E11] and 20.2% ROE [E12] could be artificially inflated. Finally, the theoretical valuation models are highly sensitive to growth assumptions that are contradicted by the near-stagnant 1% sales growth [E14], all while shareholders receive a 0.00% dividend yield [E3].
